MEMBER, MACT, KUNDAPURA, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF Rs.2,98,266/- WITH INTEREST @ 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL DEPOSIT IN TRIBUNAL.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by respondent No.2-Insurance company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V. Act') challenging the judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional NC: 2023:KHC:41212
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura
2. For the sake of convenience, parties herein are referred with the original ranks occupied by them before the Trial Court.

3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that on 01.06.2013 at about 10.30 am the deceased Mr.Appu Achari was standing in front of Prabhu Ice Cream Parlour, Municipal Road, Kundapura,
Kundapura Taluk, and at that time, the driver of the goods-Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-20-C-6212, drove it in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
As a result, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Chinmayi Hospital, Kundapura and he has taken treatment as in patient from 01.06.2013 to 20.06.2013.
Thereafter, he was treated as an out-patient.
The deceased suffered major fracture injuries and he did not recover.
The doctor NC: 2023:KHC:41212 advised that his condition was critical and there is no chance of survival.

Later on, the deceased succumbed because of the injuries The Branch Manager vs Smt Bhavani on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34781973/
2 on 13.08.2013 in his residence due to accidental injuries.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Smt Bhavani on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner claims, to have spent an huge amount for medical treatment and funeral expenses and there is loss of bread earner in the family.
Hence, they filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.9,30,000/-.
4. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle though appeared, did not contest the matter by filing objection statement.
While respondent No.2 admitted the policy of goods-Auto Rikshaw and further asserted that liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

He has denied that the accident is because of rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Auto Rikshaw and it is asserted that the accident is because of negligence on the part of the deceased.
It is further asserted that the driver of the offending vehicle did not NC: 2023:KHC:41212 possess valid and effective driving license and hence, respondent No.2 disputed the claim.
5. On the basis of these pleadings and after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has held that there is no nexus between the death and accidental injuries.
However, on the basis of loss of estate a compensation of Rs.2,98,266/- came to be awarded.
Further, the liability was fastened on the Insurance Company.
6. Being aggrieved by this judgment and award, the Insurance Company-respondent No.2 is before this Court by way of this appeal.
7. Heard learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company and learned counsel for the respondents.
Perused the records.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that there is no nexus between the death and the accidental injuries as the claimant has suffered only NC: 2023:KHC:41212 fracture of right femur and doctor is also not examined to show any nexus.
He further, submits that the accident occurred on 01.06.2013 and death has occurred on 13.08.2013 that too in the house, but the medical records are not produced to prove any nexus.
He would also assert that the driver was not possessing valid and effective driving license and hence, the Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability on the Insurance company.
He would further assert that the Tribunal erred in calculating the compensation of Rs.2,14,500/- under the head of loss of estate in the absence of material evidence and by applying wrong multiplier.
Hence, he would seek for allowing the appeal.

9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent/claimant would support the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and would contend that there is evidence disclosing that within two and a half months of the accident, he died and there is nexus and hence, he would seek for dismissal of the appeal.

It is evident that the Tribunal has framed additional issue No.4 on 02.10.2015 regarding nexus between the accident and death of deceased Mr.Appu Poojari and the said issue reads as under:
 "Whether the petitioner prove the The Branch Manager vs Smt Bhavani on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34781973/
3  nexus between the accident and then  Mr.Appu Poojari?"
 11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal after analyzing the oral and documentary evidence, answered this issue in the negative holding that there is no nexus between the death and accidental injuries.
This finding is not at all challenged by the claimants.
Apart from that, the Ex.P3-Wound certificate discloses that the claimant has suffered fracture of right femur and another simple injuries.
The records further disclose that, he was admitted in the Chinmayi Hospital on 01.06.2013 and was discharged on 20.06.2013.
However, the material documents, discharge summary is not placed on record by the claimants to show that there is any nexus between the nature of injuries NC: 2023:KHC:41212 sustained and the death.
Even the same was not reported to the concerned jurisdictional Police to enable them to file any supplementary charge sheet under Section 173(8) of the M.V. Act.

Ex.P6 is the charge sheet and it discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle was charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC along with the other provisions of the M.V.
Act, 1988.
Even the doctor was not examined and though it is asserted that the doctor has intimated the critical condition of the deceased, the same was not substantiated by examining the doctor.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly held that there is no nexus between the death and the injuries sustained.
12. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.67,946/- under the head of medical expenses which is proper.
Further, under the head of loss of income during the laid up period a sum of Rs.15,820/- came to be awarded.

However, under the head of loss of estate a sum of Rs.2,14,500/- has been awarded, on the basis of the decision in North NC: 2023:KHC:41212 West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Vs. Dundappa Ramappa Rakshi Since Deceased.

entities.text: 2023:KHC:41212 West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Vs. Dundappa Ramappa Rakshi Since Deceased
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the decision reported in laws (KAR)
2005-9-12 arising out of MFA No.4772/2002.

The Full Bench of this Court in the case of Kannamma Vs. Deputy General Manager K S R T C, [1991 0 ACJ 707] [Referred To] Karnataka, has observed that loss of estate constitute medical expenses and loss of income during treatment period i.e., loss of income during laid up period and in this case the deceased was admitted on 01.06.2013 but subsequently, discharged on 20.06.2013.

entities.text: Kannamma Vs. Deputy General Manager K S R T C, [1991 0 ACJ 707] [Referred To] Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, considering the gravity of the fracture i.e to right femur he might have been prevented from attending the work for nearly three months and that period is required to be treated as laid up period.
However, he died within two and half months and hence, under the head of loss of estate, the laid up period is required to be considered for two and a half months.
The accident has occurred in the year 2013 and this Court is consistently taking the notional income of - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41212 Rs.8,000/- pm, in respect of accident occurred in the year 2013.
13. Hence, loss of income during laid up period would work out at Rs.20,000/-.

The medical expenses disclosed that the claimants have spent Rs.67,946/- towards medical expenses and The Branch Manager vs Smt Bhavani on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34781973/

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Smt Bhavani on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 considering the incidental expenses, it can be rounded upto Rs.70,000/-.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for Rs.70,000/- under the head of medical expenses and Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of income during laid up period, which would constitute loss of estate.
Hence, the claimant would be entitled for Rs.90,000/- as against Rs.2,98,266/- awarded by the Tribunal.
14. The other contention raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that the deceased was not possessing valid driving license.
Admittedly, the vehicle involved in the accident is a goods vehicle and though the driver of the offending vehicle was holding the driving license, but it was not a transport vehicle.
The evidence of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41212 RW.1 is relied in this regard.

However, this issue has been covered by the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017) 14 Supreme Court Cases 663 and it holds the field for the time being and in view of the same, it cannot be held that the driver was not possessing the valid and effective driver license and hence, the said arguments holds no water and respondent No.2/appellant herein, is liable to pay the compensation and the question of pay and recover does not arise at all.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017) 14 Supreme Court Cases 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of these facts and circumstances, the appeal needs to be allowed in part.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1.
The appeal is allowed in part.

2. The claimants are held entitled for total compensation of Rs.90,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41212 till the date of realization as against Rs.2,98,266/- awarded by the Tribunal.
3. The entire compensation is required to be paid by respondent No.2-Insurance company/appellant herein.

4. The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for disbursement and excess amount,
if any, shall be refunded to appellant herein i.e. respondent No.2 before the Tribunal after satisfying the award.
